slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
Two lines are perpendicular if they meet to form a right angle.

Theorem: perpendicular lines form four right angles.

Proof: one angle is 90 degrees. Its vertical angle is also 90 (vertical angles are equal). Each of the other two angles forms a linear pair with a 90 degree angle, so each is 180 − 90 = 90 degrees. Folding a paper edge onto itself makes a crease perpendicular to the edge for the same reason: the two angles at the crease are equal and add to 180.

slides.title: Check yourself
slides.html: If two angles of a linear pair are equal, what must each measure?
slides.reveal: They add to 180 and are equal, so each is 90 degrees, and the lines are perpendicular.
